contract: analyze(ensemble, observations, observed_indices, observation_variance) -> updated ensemble with the same (16,20) shape. Lorenz-96 dx_i/dt=(x_(i+1)-x_(i-2))*x_(i-1)-x_i+F with periodic indices, nondimensional units. Evaluator propagates each member by RK4 at dt=0.01 for five steps between updates, then observes even-indexed states with independent N(0,0.49) noise. Three runs F=6,8,10, seeds=181,283,389; 40 updates each. Score is pooled analysis-mean RMSE against independent DOP853 truth over all states and cycles. Output must be finite and within [-100,100]. Use assimilation_case with seeds=41,53,67 for development; no truth or future observations are provided to analyze.
notes: Reduced deterministic Lorenz-96 twin experiment inspired by Tomizawa and Sawada (2021), Section 2. Local choices: 20 states, 16 members, perfect-model forcing, partial observations, short horizon and deterministic initial seeds. No reservoir computer is required. This is neither real weather nor a reproduction of the paper's scores. All evaluation seeds are public; use new seeds after freezing a candidate to assess generalization.
protocol_description: Reimplemented in this repository from the paper's task description; instances are generated locally with a fixed seed, so scores are comparable within the suite but not with the paper's numbers.
name: Climate dynamics: partial-observation Lorenz-96 assimilation
description: Design an ensemble analysis update that reconstructs an evolving twenty-variable chaotic state from noisy observations of half its coordinates. The evaluator propagates the ensemble and compares each updated ensemble mean with independent high-accuracy reference trajectories.
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Tomizawa and Sawada (2021), Combining ensemble Kalman filter and reservoir computing to predict spatiotemporal chaotic systems; Section 2.1 Eq. (1) Lorenz-96 dynamics and Section 2.2 ensemble data assimilation.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic twin experiments, not weather observations or the paper's reservoir-computing results.
Local reduced dimensions, seeds, observation noise, spin-up, perfect-model forcing and short duration are documented in the contract. Longer-horizon stability and forecast skill are not established.
All evaluation seeds are public. Use fresh seeds and forcing regimes after freezing the candidate for a generalization claim.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Reconstruct the hidden state of a reduced chaotic Lorenz-96 system from partial noisy observations.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Data assimilation has substantive geoscience uses, but an arbitrary reduced chaotic test does not inherit those uses automatically.
science_relevance.reason: The cited paper combines ensemble Kalman filtering and reservoir computing and uses Lorenz-96 as a method demonstration. The local twenty-variable synthetic twin experiment is still a methodological testbed, with no inspected primary paper pursuing its exact state reconstruction as a substantive scientific or real-world question. No qualifying primary-goal evidence is established for this local task in this review; this is not a finding that the broader subject is unimportant.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Local task contract and cited source purpose reviewed; background or benchmark citations were not promoted to primary-problem evidence.
